name: New South Wales
rule: Domestic rabbits can be kept as pets; keeping wild rabbits is not allowed.

name: Victoria
rule: Domestic rabbits can be kept as pets; wild rabbits are a declared pest.

name: Queensland
rule: Keeping, selling or bringing a rabbit into Queensland is illegal under the Biosecurity Act 2014. Maximum penalty: 500 penalty units.

name: South Australia
rule: By law, pet rabbits must live in an escape-proof cage or pen, must not roam the property and must never be released.

name: Western Australia
rule: Domestic breeds can be kept without a permit, but brown, wild-type rabbits can't be kept or brought into the state.

name: Tasmania
rule: Pet rabbits can be kept on mainland Tasmania and Bruny Island, but taking one to any other Tasmanian island is banned.

name: Northern Territory
rule: Domestic rabbits are listed among animals that do not need a permit.

name: Australian Capital Territory
rule: Owners must follow a mandatory code of practice (2024) covering housing, food, health and care.
